newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa to have heart test.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa to have heart test.

text.p: Mother Teresa, in hospital with a recurrent chest pain, has agreed to undergo a special radiological test this week to see if an artery in her heart is blocked and an operation is needed, her doctor said on Tuesday.

Dr S.K. Sen, of the Woodlands Nursing Home in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta, said the 86-year-old nun would be moved to a nearby heart clinic for an angiography, an X-ray of blood vessels to see if she has a blocked artery.
Mother Teresa, who was fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989, has twice undergone coronary angiography, once in 1991 in the United States and a second time in 1993 in Calcutta.
In both cases she subsequently underwent angioplasty, in which surgeons inserted a balloon into her artery to unblock it.
Woodlands Nursing Home said in a medical bulletin results of the angiography would determine whether she needed surgery.

Sen said Mother Teresa would be moved to Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre, probably on Tuesday afternoon, for the angiography, which would be performed in a day or two. Dr Patricia Aubanel, who treated her in the United States, has arrived in Calcutta to help supervise the procedure, he said
